$comment: SHIPPED naming contract — the generic half. Everything here is company-agnostic and safe to publish: generic areas, the slug shape, and the detector vocabularies. The ORG's own domain words and their area mapping are NOT here; they live in the org brain's schemas/node-types.json (domains.registry), which is PR-gated. That split is what keeps this repo free of any organisation's fingerprints.

areas.$comment: Three families. Business = what the organisation does (APQC PCF level-1 anchored). Technical = what it builds and runs on, named generically so no vendor appears. Product = this toolchain, because notes about the tool are the first notes anyone writes. Vertical packs add more; an industrial pack adds production/inventory/quality/assets/safety.

severity.$comment: Only an unregistered domain is an error. Everything else warns and the write still succeeds — a refusal makes an author drop the fact or fake a name to get past the gate, which is worse than a bad name.

$comment_domainRequiredIn: Only knowledge nodes carry a domain. reports/ and plans/ are dated artifacts and raw/ is undigested capture — requiring a domain there would flag correct names.

claimShape.$comment: A name that states a verdict is unstable by construction: correct the claim and the name lies. Three signals, measured at 19% of a 126-node corpus.

findTarget.$comment: The lookup is mandatory — no node is created without a result in hand — but the ACTION is graded, and slug text alone never triggers an update. Evidence: two notes scored 0.595 on slug similarity and are entirely different facts (one says a reload leg is ADF rather than a pipeline, the other says that reload needs four pre-existing framework tables). A false merge is worse than a fork, because a fork is visible.

meaningGuard.$comment: Never auto-apply a rename that drops a word appearing in this many nodes or fewer. Rarity was tried as a name GENERATOR and rejected — with six words tied at frequency 1 the tie-break went alphabetical and dropped a proper noun, and cluster terms are frequent precisely because they name something real, so rarity demoted the identifying words. It works as a guard.
